brief: The courtyard is the title object and has been untouched since #95, the longest gap in the town, and the person who tends it is nearly never there. Measured at #94: gardener presence is a 13 h mean of 0.17 in summer, 0 in winter, and above zero in only 5 of 30 samples - despite 0.7 set-outs a day. The cause named at #95 is a one-at-a-time rule plus long walks, and the fix it suggested is a gardener who arrives EARLY (a sunrise set-out through a short door) or a second bed slot. Make the courtyard visibly tended: someone in it, working, for a real share of the daylight.
successLooksLike: Summer gardener presence over 13 h rises materially above HEAD's 0.17 mean and winter stops being a flat zero, reported for HEAD and candidate from the same probe on the same seeds. Measure PRESENCE over folded time, not a per-instant crop.
avoid: Do not add a new kind of worker, and do not raise the set-out rate - 0.7/day is already fine and the fault is presence, not arrivals. Price presence as rate x visit before you touch any cap: lengthen the stay or shorten the walk. Do not let a longer stay block the bed the way the one-at-a-time rule already does; release the bed as the walk out begins.
